newsitem.title: INDIA: India NSE detects fake shares of 40 million rupees.
newsitem.headline: India NSE detects fake shares of 40 million rupees.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) has uncovered fake shares totalling 40 million rupees, a senior NSE official said on Thursday.
The official, who did not want to be identified, said the concerned broker member had already replaced shares worth 10 million rupees.

"The member has assured us that they are making whatever effort they can to cover it and repay it. As long as they are replacing or rectifying it, where is the question of doing anything," he told Reuters.
He said the fake shares -- which were introduced some time earlier this year -- had been uncovered recently.
"It's been fairly recent. We've been getting complaints for the last couple of weeks," he said.
The official said newspaper reports that fake shares worth 400 million rupees were circulating on the exchange were exaggerated.
The total amount of forged share certificates discovered by the NSE in the last couple of years is estimated at around 110 million rupees, the official said.
